Description: The authoritative, normative specification defining Ethereum’s Proof-of-Stake consensus rules, including fork choice, finality, validator duties, slashing conditions, and upgrade encoding.
Reason for inclusion:
- Defines the canonical rules that all Ethereum consensus clients must implement
- Serves as the single source of truth for consensus behavior
- Governs how consensus-level upgrades are specified and activated
- Ensures deterministic convergence across independent client implementations
Supported Networks:
- Ethereum Mainnet
- Ethereum Testnets (e.g., Goerli, Sepolia, Holesky)
- Future Ethereum networks via fork upgrades
License: Creative Commons / Open Specification (non-code normative spec; code references under permissive licenses)
Role in Consensus:
- Defines fork choice rules and finality mechanics
- Specifies validator duties, rewards, and penalties
- Encodes consensus-level upgrades and fork transitions
- Acts as the authoritative reference for all consensus clients
Implementation language: N/A (Specification-level; implemented by clients in multiple languages)
Practictioners Note: Ethereum’s consensus is spec-driven rather than client-driven. Independent clients compete on implementation quality but must strictly converge on this specification. This separation is a core safety property of the Ethereum protocol.
Practioner Validation Check:
If Ethereum Consensus Specifications disappeared:
- Consensus clients would lose their canonical reference
- Network upgrades would be impossible to coordinate safely
- Consensus behavior would fragment, risking chain splits and loss of finality

Description: A production-grade Ethereum consensus client written in Go, implementing Ethereum’s Proof-of-Stake consensus rules and validator duties.
Reason for inclusion:
- Implements Ethereum’s Proof-of-Stake consensus specification
- Directly participates in fork choice, attestations, and finality
- Historically used by a large share of Ethereum validators
- Enforces canonical consensus rules at the protocol level
Supported Networks:
- Ethereum Mainnet
- Ethereum Testnets (e.g., Goerli, Sepolia, Holesky)
Client Implementation: Ethereum Consensus Client (Beacon Node + Validator Client)
Role in Consensus:
- Executes fork choice rules
- Coordinates validator duties (proposals, attestations)
- Participates in finality via Casper FFG
- Enforces slashing and inactivity penalties
Practictioners Note: Prysm’s dominance during earlier PoS phases made client diversity a live protocol risk. Practioner Validation Check:
If Prysm disappeared:
- A large portion of validators would be affected
- Client diversity would shift materially
- Consensus participation would require immediate operator coordination
